name: Sword Draw
description: Draw the blade on an outbreath and cut once so a thin edge of sword qi follows the steel through the target.

name: Blade Guard
description: Hold the blade across the body with qi spread along the flat so a blow lands on it and goes no further.

name: Blade Breath
description: Breathe slowly with the blade upright until qi gathers in the edge and the wielder's next few cuts bite deeper.

name: Tip Advance
description: Slide one pace forward behind the point of the blade so the body follows the sword into the gap.

name: Level Cut
description: Swing the blade flat and level at chest height with qi riding the edge from hilt to tip.

name: Quiet Thrust
description: Drive the point straight at the target in one silent push with the qi gathered at the tip.

name: Rising Draw
description: Pull the sword upward out of the scabbard in a slanting cut that carries a thin line of qi along the edge.

name: Falling Cut
description: Bring the blade down from above the head in one straight stroke with the qi sinking into the edge.

name: Slip Edge
description: Meet an incoming blade with the edge turned slightly aside so it slides off along a film of qi.

name: Brief Thrust
description: Push the point forward a hand's breadth with a snap of the wrist and a spark of qi at the tip.

name: Hilt Strike
description: Drive the pommel into the target at close range with qi packed into the hilt for a stunning blow.

name: Back Step
description: Draw the rear foot behind the lead and withdraw one pace with the point still aimed at the target.

name: Sheath Hold
description: Raise the scabbard with the blade still inside and let a blow break upon it with qi packed along its length.

name: Breath Before Cut
description: Hold a full breath until the qi settles then let it out through a single cut that carries the whole exhale.

name: Sword Calm
description: Draw even breaths in time with the sword's slow motion so the wielder's qi flows smoothly into every cut.

name: Sword Rest
description: Lower the blade to a resting guard and breathe out so a calm shell of qi covers the body.

name: Reaching Thrust
description: Extend the whole arm and the blade in one line so the point reaches a pace beyond the usual thrust.

name: Outbreath Step
description: Step on the outbreath so the body glides a pace to the side while the sword stays level.

name: Qi Edge
description: Coat the blade in a thin sheath of qi and cut so the edge bites deeper than bare steel can.

name: Edge Flare
description: Flare the qi on the edge at the instant of contact so the cut lands with a sudden bright bite.

name: Thin Edge
description: Narrow the qi along the edge to a hair's width and slip it through a gap in the target's guard.

name: Edge Wake
description: Flick the blade so a short crescent of qi leaves the edge and flies a few paces ahead of the cut.

name: Qi Parry
description: Meet a strike with the qi-coated flat of the blade and turn its force off to the side.

name: Edge Coil
description: Spin the blade in slow circles so a ring of edge qi forms about the body and turns light blows.

name: Edge Slide
description: Slide the lead foot along the line of the blade so the body shifts with the edge and stays balanced.

name: Qi Flick
description: Flick the point at the target's sword wrist so a jolt of qi rattles the grip and spoils the next stroke.

name: Sheath Draw
description: Draw from the scabbard in the same motion as the cut so the blade is already moving when it clears.

name: Sheath Press
description: Press the scabbard mouth against the target's hand to stop a draw before the blade clears.

name: Scabbard Guard
description: Swing the scabbard across the body to catch a blow on its lacquered length wrapped in qi.

name: Quick Return
description: Turn aside a thrust with the flat then slide the blade home into its scabbard and ready the draw.

name: Drawing Stride
description: Step through the target's flank with the hand on the hilt so the draw comes as the foot lands.

name: Still Hand
description: Rest the hand on the hilt and let qi spread along the scabbard to feel the reach and weight of a nearby blade.

name: Leading Point
description: Let the point travel first and the body follow so the thrust arrives before the target can read it.

name: Point Flick
description: Snap the tip across the target's hand or face in a short cut and return it to guard.

name: Point Advance
description: Advance along the line the point is drawing so the feet never cross the line of the thrust.

name: Point Ward
description: Tap an incoming blade with the tip at its weakest point and push it off its line.

name: Needle Thrust
description: Pack the qi into a point no wider than a needle and punch it through a seam in the target's defense.

name: Point Ring
description: Circle the tip around the target's blade and wrench it aside with a ring of qi at the point.

name: Tip Qi
description: Loose a thumb-sized bead of qi from the tip of the blade straight at the target.

name: Steel Ward
description: Raise the sword upright before the body with qi along the blade so one blow is taken without harm.

name: Flat Block
description: Turn the flat of the blade to the blow and brace with the whole forearm so the strike stops.

name: Rolling Ward
description: Roll the blade over the striker's weapon so the blow slides along the steel and past the body.

name: Guard Into Cut
description: Turn the held guard into a cut in one motion so the answer leaves the blade as the blow ends.

name: Guarded Stride
description: Step back a pace with the sword still held in guard so distance opens without breaking the line.

name: Firm Footwork
description: Advance with the weight low and even so the blade never wavers as the feet close the distance.

name: Blade Turn
description: Turn the edge over mid-stroke so the cut changes line and lands from the other side.

name: Pivot Cut
description: Pivot on the lead heel and swing the blade round the turn so the weight of the body drives the edge.

name: Slide Guard
description: Slide off the line of attack and let the blade guide the blow past the shoulder.

name: Sweep Low
description: Sweep the edge close to the ground to cut the shins and bring the target's guard down.

name: Rear Step
description: Pull the rear foot back and shift the weight so the body draws away and the sword stays forward.

name: Close Draw
description: Draw the sword at chest range with a short elbow cut that gives the target no room to answer.

name: Weight Settle
description: Move the weight from one foot to the other in time with the edge so the cut leaves no opening behind.

name: Sword Reach Sense
description: Spread a thin web of qi along the blade to feel how far a stranger's weapon can reach.

name: Hilt Sense
description: Grip the hilt and let qi run through the palm to read the tension in a nearby swordsman's hands.

name: Guard Read
description: Touch blades once and read from the shiver of qi where the other sword's guard is thin.

name: Steadied Hilt
description: Breathe out and still the sword hand so a gathered pulse of qi makes the next cut more exact.

name: Sense Cut
description: Cut at the point the sense has marked as weakest and follow the qi trace straight into the opening.

name: Warning Ward
description: Raise the blade the instant the sword sense tingles and let a quick shell of qi take the first blow.

name: Rising Cut
description: Cut upward from the hip through the target's guard with qi lifting along the edge.

name: Upward Draw
description: Draw the sword in a steep rising arc that opens the target's arm and lifts its blade away.

name: Lift Ward
description: Raise the blade under an overhead cut and lift it off line with a rising swell of qi.

name: High Cut
description: Rise onto the toes and cut at head height with the edge angled to catch the neck guard.

name: Spring Step
description: Push off the rear foot in a light upward step that carries the body past a low cut.

name: Rise Break
description: Catch the underside of the target's blade with a rising cut and knock it high to break the stroke.

name: Lifting Thrust
description: Thrust upward at a slant beneath the ribs with the qi carried on the rising line of the point.
